hints: Look closely at the right-hand carbon in the ring, the OH group is pointing down below the ring. What does that tell you about alpha versus beta glucose?
Remember what each named carbohydrate is made from: amylopectin and glycogen are both glucose polymers, and sucrose is glucose plus fructose.
walkthrough:
**Identify the monomer from the diagram**

Look at this six-sided ring, it is a hexose sugar with formula $C_6H_{12}O_6$. The key clue is carbon 1 on the right side.

The OH on carbon 1 is pointing down, and the $CH_2OH$ group is pointing up. That is the classic pattern for alpha-glucose.

**Check which molecules use alpha-glucose**

Amylopectin is a branched plant starch made only from alpha-glucose joined by 1,4 and 1,6 glycosidic bonds. Glycogen is the branched animal store, also made only from alpha-glucose.

Sucrose is a disaccharide made from alpha-glucose joined to fructose. So all three molecules contain this same monomer.

**Read the Venn diagram**

Region A is amylopectin and glycogen only. Region C is amylopectin and sucrose only. Region D is sucrose only.

Region B is the centre where all three circles overlap. Since all three contain alpha-glucose, the answer is B.

options.A: This is only the overlap of amylopectin and glycogen. It leaves out sucrose, but sucrose also contains alpha-glucose.
options.B: This is the centre overlap of all three. Amylopectin, glycogen and sucrose all contain alpha-glucose, so this is correct.
options.C: This is only the overlap of amylopectin and sucrose. It leaves out glycogen, but glycogen is also made from alpha-glucose.
options.D: This is sucrose only. It is wrong because amylopectin and glycogen also contain this monomer, not just sucrose.
